Canaan Dog.summary: An ancient pariah breed from the Middle East, re-established in the 1930s from semi-wild desert dogs to work as a guard and herding dog.
funFacts: It's the national dog of Israel.
Dogs of this type have survived on their own in the Negev desert for thousands of years.

Cane Corso.summary: A large Italian mastiff descended from Roman war dogs, used for centuries to guard property and hunt big game.
funFacts: Its name roughly means "bodyguard dog," from the Latin "cohors" (guardian).
The breed nearly vanished in the 20th century and was revived by Italian enthusiasts in the 1970s.

Cardigan Welsh Corgi.summary: The older of the two corgi breeds, a low-slung Welsh cattle dog distinguished by its long, foxy tail.
funFacts: Unlike the Pembroke, the Cardigan has a long tail and larger, rounder ears.
"Corgi" is usually translated from Welsh as "dwarf dog."

Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.summary: A gentle toy spaniel descended from the lapdogs of English royalty, especially King Charles II.
funFacts: King Charles II was said to take his spaniels almost everywhere, even to council meetings.
The red-and-white "Blenheim" color is named after Blenheim Palace.

Cavapoo.summary: A cross between a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and a toy or miniature Poodle, bred as a gentle, lower-shedding companion.
funFacts: In Australia it's called the Cavoodle and is one of the country's most popular dogs.
Its coat can be wavy or tightly curled, depending on which parent it takes after.

Chesapeake Bay Retriever.summary: A powerful American retriever bred to haul ducks out of the icy waters of the Chesapeake Bay.
funFacts: The breed descends from two Newfoundland puppies rescued from a sinking ship off Maryland in 1807.
Its oily, wavy double coat is almost waterproof.
It's the state dog of Maryland.

Chihuahua.summary: The world's smallest dog breed, named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua and probably descended from the Techichi dogs of ancient Mexico.
funFacts: Chihuahuas have the largest brain relative to body size of any dog breed.
Many are born with a soft spot on the skull, called a molera, like a human baby.

Chinese Crested.summary: An elegant toy breed that comes in two varieties in the same litter: the mostly hairless Hairless and the fully coated Powderpuff.
Chinese Crested.origin: China (likely older African or Mexican roots)
funFacts: Hairless and Powderpuff puppies can be born in the same litter.
Chinese Cresteds have won the World's Ugliest Dog Contest several times.

Chow Chow.summary: An ancient Chinese breed with a lion-like mane and an aloof, almost cat-like personality.
funFacts: Chow Chows have blue-black tongues.
Sigmund Freud's Chow, Jofi, often sat in on his therapy sessions.

Clumber Spaniel.summary: The heaviest of the spaniels, a long, low, mostly white gundog developed at Clumber Park, the Duke of Newcastle's estate.
funFacts: It's named after Clumber Park in Nottinghamshire.
King Edward VII kept Clumbers at the royal Sandringham estate.

Cockapoo.summary: A cross between a Cocker Spaniel and a Poodle, one of the oldest "designer" dogs, dating back to the 1950s in the United States.
funFacts: It's considered one of the first popular designer crossbreeds.
In the UK, Cockapoos regularly rank among the most popular dogs.

Cocker Spaniel.summary: The smallest of the AKC's sporting dogs, a merry American spaniel with a long, silky coat, developed from the English Cocker.
funFacts: Lady in Disney's Lady and the Tramp is an American Cocker Spaniel.
"Cocker" comes from their use in hunting woodcock.

Collie.summary: A graceful Scottish herding dog with a flowing coat, made world-famous by the Lassie films and TV series.
funFacts: Lassie was played by male Collies, starting with a dog named Pal.
Queen Victoria helped make Collies fashionable in the 1860s.

Curly-Coated Retriever.summary: One of the oldest retriever breeds, covered in tight, crisp curls that shed water and brambles.
funFacts: It's the tallest of the retriever breeds.
Its tight curls protect it in icy water and thick cover.

Dachshund.summary: A long-bodied, short-legged German hound bred to dig into badger dens, now one of the world's most popular companions.
funFacts: "Dachshund" means "badger dog" in German.
A Dachshund named Waldi was the first official Olympic mascot (Munich, 1972).
They come in three coat types: smooth, wirehaired and longhaired.

Dalmatian.summary: A spotted coach dog named after Dalmatia in Croatia, famous for running alongside horse-drawn carriages and fire engines.
funFacts: Dalmatian puppies are born pure white; their spots appear as they grow.
They became firehouse mascots because they guarded and calmed the horses that pulled fire wagons.

Dandie Dinmont Terrier.summary: A long, low terrier from the Scottish Borders with a big, fluffy topknot, bred to hunt otters and badgers.
funFacts: It's the only breed named after a fictional character: Dandie Dinmont in Sir Walter Scott's 1815 novel Guy Mannering.
It's one of the rarest terrier breeds today.

Dingo.summary: Australia's wild dog, descended from domestic dogs that arrived with people thousands of years ago and returned to the wild.
funFacts: The Dingo Fence, built to keep dingoes away from sheep, stretches about 5,600 km across Australia.
Dingoes have unusually flexible joints and can rotate their wrists and climb.

Doberman Pinscher.summary: A sleek, powerful guard dog developed in Germany in the 1890s. Dobermans are loyal, alert and highly trainable.
funFacts: Tax collector Louis Dobermann bred the first Dobermans to protect him on his rounds.
A Doberman named Kurt is honored at the U.S. War Dog Cemetery on Guam after dying in the 1944 battle there.

Dogue de Bordeaux.summary: A massive French mastiff with a huge head and a red coat, used historically to guard estates and drive cattle.
funFacts: Hooch, Tom Hanks's co-star in Turner & Hooch (1989), was a Dogue de Bordeaux.
It has one of the largest heads relative to its body of any breed.

English Bulldog.summary: A stocky, wrinkled English breed with a pushed-in face, once used in bull-baiting and later reshaped into a gentle, calm companion.
funFacts: The Bulldog is the mascot of the U.S. Marine Corps and many universities, including Yale.
Because of their large heads, most Bulldog puppies are born by C-section.

English Cocker Spaniel.summary: A compact British gundog bred to flush and retrieve woodcock, a little taller and leaner than its American cousin.
funFacts: The AKC split the English and American Cocker into separate breeds in 1946.
Its constantly wagging tail earned it the nickname "merry cocker."

English Foxhound.summary: A sturdy pack hound bred for centuries by English hunts, with breeding records going back to the 1700s.
funFacts: Some English Foxhound packs have stud books dating back to the 1700s.
It's one of the least common breeds registered with the AKC.

English Setter.summary: A gentle, elegant bird dog with a speckled coat, bred to "set" (crouch) when it finds game birds.
funFacts: Its speckled coat pattern is called "belton," after a village in Northumberland.
Setters got their name from crouching low to show hunters where birds were hiding.

English Springer Spaniel.summary: A medium-sized British gundog bred to "spring" (flush) game birds into the air for hunters.
funFacts: Millie, George H. W. Bush's Springer, "wrote" a bestselling book about life in the White House.
Springers are widely used as detection dogs by police and customs agencies.

English Toy Spaniel.summary: A small, flat-faced spaniel, called the King Charles Spaniel in the UK, that has been a royal lapdog since the Tudor era.
funFacts: In the 1920s, breeders recreated the longer-nosed spaniels in old paintings, giving rise to the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.
Legend says Mary, Queen of Scots had her toy spaniel with her at her execution.

Entlebucher Mountain Dog.summary: The smallest of the four Swiss mountain dogs, a nimble tricolor cattle herder from the Entlebuch valley.
funFacts: It's the smallest of the four Swiss Sennenhund breeds.
The AKC recognized it only in 2011.

Field Spaniel.summary: A rare, medium-sized British spaniel with a glossy coat, bred to hunt birds in dense cover.
funFacts: The breed nearly disappeared in the early 1900s after being bred for exaggerated length.
It's one of the rarest sporting breeds registered with the AKC.

Fila Brasileiro.summary: A huge Brazilian mastiff known for its tracking ability and fierce devotion to its family.
funFacts: It moves both legs on one side at the same time, a "camel pace" that's unusual in dogs.
It's banned or restricted in several countries, including the UK.

Finnish Spitz.summary: Finland's national dog, a fox-red spitz that hunts birds by barking to mark the tree where they perch.
funFacts: Finland holds barking contests for the breed; top barkers can bark more than 100 times a minute.
It's the national dog of Finland.

Flat-Coated Retriever.summary: A sleek black or liver retriever known for its lifelong, puppy-like enthusiasm.
funFacts: Owners call it the "Peter Pan" of retrievers because it never seems to grow up.
It was England's most popular retriever before the Labrador and Golden took over.

French Bulldog.summary: A compact companion with signature "bat ears," developed in France from toy bulldogs brought over by English lace workers.
funFacts: In 2022 it became America's most popular breed, ending the Labrador's 31-year run.
Most Frenchies can't swim well because of their heavy front ends.

German Pinscher.summary: A sleek, medium-sized German ratter and watchdog, and an ancestor of the Doberman and the Miniature Pinscher.
funFacts: It helped create both the Doberman Pinscher and the Miniature Pinscher.
The breed nearly disappeared after the two World Wars.

German Shepherd.summary: A versatile, intelligent German herding dog that has become the world's leading police, military and service dog.
funFacts: The breed was founded by Captain Max von Stephanitz in 1899.
Rin Tin Tin, rescued from a World War I battlefield, became a Hollywood star.
The first U.S. guide dog for the blind, Buddy, was a German Shepherd.

German Shorthaired Pointer.summary: An all-purpose German hunting dog that points, retrieves and tracks on land and in water.
funFacts: A GSP named CJ won Best in Show at Westminster in 2016.
Their webbed feet make them strong swimmers.

German Wirehaired Pointer.summary: A rugged, all-weather German gundog with a wiry, water-resistant coat and a distinctive beard.
funFacts: In Germany it's called the Deutsch Drahthaar and is one of the most popular hunting dogs.
Its harsh coat protects it from brambles and icy water.

Giant Schnauzer.summary: The largest of the three schnauzers, developed in Bavaria to drive cattle and later used as a police and guard dog.
funFacts: It was once known as the Munich Schnauzer.
"Schnauzer" comes from the German word for snout.

Glen of Imaal Terrier.summary: A short-legged, sturdy Irish terrier from the remote Glen of Imaal in County Wicklow.
funFacts: Glens were reportedly used as "turnspit dogs," running in wheels to turn meat roasting over a fire.
It's one of the rarest terrier breeds in the world.

Golden Retriever.summary: A friendly, eager-to-please Scottish gundog bred to retrieve waterfowl, now one of the world's most popular family dogs.
funFacts: The breed was developed by Lord Tweedmouth in the Scottish Highlands in the mid-1800s.
Goldens have such a "soft mouth" that many can carry a raw egg without breaking it.

Goldendoodle.summary: A cross between a Golden Retriever and a Poodle, popular since the 1990s as a friendly, lower-shedding family dog.
funFacts: Breeders use labels like F1 (Golden × Poodle) and F1B (F1 × Poodle) to describe the mix.
Goldendoodles come in toy, miniature, medium and standard sizes.
